## Further Reading

American Institute of Certified Public Accountants. (2025). *Audit sampling: Audit guide*. <https://www.aicpa-cima.com/cpe-learning/publication/audit-sampling-audit-guide> The practitioner's guide to statistical and nonstatistical sampling in audits, with step-by-step guidance, tables, and case studies. It sets out the judgments behind a sample of the kind Requirement 6 plans: the risk accepted, the deviations tolerated, and how to evaluate what the sample finds.

Association of Certified Fraud Examiners. (2026). *Occupational fraud 2026: A report to the nations*. <https://www.acfe.com/fraud-resources/report-to-the-nations> The ACFE's study of more than two thousand occupational fraud cases from over a hundred countries. It finds asset misappropriation in nine cases out of ten, and associates anti-fraud controls with lower losses and earlier detection, which is the case for the detective tests this chapter builds.

Cohen, J. R., Joe, J. R., Thibodeau, J. C., & Trompeter, G. M. (2020). Audit partners' judgments and challenges in the audits of internal control over financial reporting. *Auditing: A Journal of Practice & Theory*, *39*(4), 57–85. <https://doi.org/10.2308/ajpt-18-088> Interviews with twenty audit partners about how they evaluate control deficiencies. The partners describe managers who find it hard to accept that a material weakness can exist without a detected error and who argue that a review control would have caught the problem, the pushback Requirement 9 asks you to anticipate.

Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission & Association of Certified Fraud Examiners. (2023). *Fraud risk management guide* (2nd ed.). <https://www.aicpa-cima.com/cpe-learning/publication/fraud-risk-management-guide> A blueprint for an organization's fraud risk management program, from governance and risk assessment to preventive and detective controls and the monitoring of the program. The second edition expanded its treatment of data analytics and explains how fraud risk management relates to internal control.

Elder, R. J., Akresh, A. D., Glover, S. M., Higgs, J. L., & Liljegren, J. (2013). Audit sampling research: A synthesis and implications for future research. *Auditing: A Journal of Practice & Theory*, *32*(Suppl. 1), 99–129. <https://doi.org/10.2308/ajpt-50394> A synthesis of research on the decisions auditors make when they sample: whether sampling applies, which kind, how large a sample, and how to evaluate the errors found. It reports that auditors may understate risk to reduce testing and sometimes fail to project the errors in a sample, cautions worth keeping beside @tbl-19-03.

Institute of Internal Auditors. (2024). *Global internal audit standards*. <https://www.theiia.org/en/standards/2024-standards/global-internal-audit-standards/> The standards that govern internal auditing, in effect since January 2025. Their domain on performing engagements covers how internal auditors evaluate the significance of findings, develop recommendations and action plans with management, and communicate the results, the work of Requirements 8 and 9.

Public Company Accounting Oversight Board. (n.d.-a). *AS 2201: An audit of internal control over financial reporting that is integrated with an audit of financial statements*. <https://pcaobus.org/oversight/standards/auditing-standards/details/AS2201> The standard for integrated audits of public companies. Its appendix defines a control deficiency, a significant deficiency, and a material weakness, and its section on evaluating identified deficiencies explains how likelihood, magnitude, compensating controls, and combination decide a deficiency's severity.
